Wadi Ghadir magnetics – 3-D susceptibility inversion with SimPEG¶

Wadi Ghadir, Eastern Desert, Egypt · total-field magnetic anomaly (TMI − IGRF-14)

Written by Mohamed Sobh, LIAG (Leibniz Institute for Applied Geophysics)

This notebook inverts the ground-magnetic readings of Wadi Ghadir for a 3-D magnetic-susceptibility model with SimPEG. It is the second of three:

Notebook Data Unknown
06 gravity stations, complete Bouguer anomaly density contrast Δρ [g/cm³]
07 (this one) magnetic readings, total-field anomaly magnetic susceptibility χ [SI]
08 both Δρ and χ together, coupled by a cross-gradient term

All three use the same mesh, topography and data preparation (wghadir/inversion.py).

The steps

Step Content
1 Load the accepted readings and the inducing field (magnetic chain, table 30)
2 Remove a regional trend
3 Thin the 12 000 readings (block median) and assign uncertainties
4 Topography and the 3-D tensor mesh (as in notebook 06)
5 Survey, forward simulation and sensitivity
6 The inversion with χ ≥ 0; run
7 Data fit
8 The susceptibility model: depth slices, cross-sections and comparison with the RTP map
9 Export

Assumptions. Magnetisation is induced by today's field (F ≈ 41 970 nT, I ≈ 36.7°, D ≈ 4.2°, IGRF-14) and proportional to χ; remanence and self-demagnetisation are ignored. Magnetic data resolve depth even more poorly than gravity data; the model is the simplest one that fits the data, not the true geology.

Each step has ✏️ PARAMETERS, ▶ PROCESSING and 📊 RESULT cells. The notebook runs in about a minute.

1 The readings and the inducing field¶

The magnetic chain (wghadir.chains.MagneticChain, outputs/tables/30_mag_readings_qc.csv) provides every reading with its position, elevation, quality flags and the total-field anomaly TMA = TMI − IGRF-14 (survey date assumed 20 January 2026). Only accepted readings (spikes removed by the Hampel filter) are used. The inducing field is the IGRF-14 at the survey: its strength, inclination and declination define how a susceptible body is magnetised.

In [2]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
SENSOR_HEIGHT_M = 2.0      # magnetometer sensor above the ground
In [3]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
mag, FIELD = W.load_magnetics(REPO, sensor_m=SENSOR_HEIGHT_M)
print(f"{len(mag):,} accepted readings; TMA {mag.tma.min():.0f} … {mag.tma.max():.0f} nT (median {mag.tma.median():.0f} nT)")
print(f"inducing field: F = {FIELD['F']:.0f} nT, I = {FIELD['I']:.2f}°, D = {FIELD['D']:.2f}°")

2 Regional trend¶

The IGRF removes the core field, but a smooth trend of the crustal field remains (and any error of the assumed date appears as a constant). A low-order polynomial surface fitted to all readings is removed, so that the inversion explains local anomalies. TREND_DEGREE = 0 removes only the median.

In [5]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
TREND_DEGREE = 1          # 0: median only, 1: plane, 2: quadratic surface
In [6]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
mag["trend"] = W.polynomial_trend(mag.e.values, mag.n.values, mag.tma.values, TREND_DEGREE) if TREND_DEGREE > 0 else mag.tma.median()
mag["residual"] = mag.tma - mag.trend
print(f"trend {np.min(mag.trend):.0f} … {np.max(mag.trend):.0f} nT; residual {mag.residual.min():.0f} … {mag.residual.max():.0f} nT")

trend -305 … 44 nT; residual -1467 … 2068 nT

# 📊 RESULT
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.6))
for ax, col, title in ((axes[0], "trend", f"trend (degree {TREND_DEGREE})"), (axes[1], "residual", "residual = data for the inversion")):
    v = mag[col]
    sc = ax.scatter(mag.e / 1000, mag.n / 1000, c=v, s=2, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=np.percentile(v, 2), vmax=np.percentile(v, 98))
    ax.set(aspect="equal", title=title, xlabel="easting [km]")
    plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="nT", shrink=0.75)
axes[0].set_ylabel("northing [km]")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

3 Thinning and uncertainties¶

The readings are about 3 m apart along the tracks, 100 times closer than the cells. One median per BLOCK_M block reduces them to a few hundred robust values. The uncertainty is a floor plus a fraction of the value: the floor covers the diurnal-correction error (crossovers of a few nT), positioning, and the short-wavelength geological noise that a 400 m mesh cannot represent.

In [8]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
BLOCK_M = 400.0
FLOOR_NT = 10.0
PERCENT = 0.05
In [9]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
mb = W.block_median(mag, ["residual"], BLOCK_M)
mb["data"] = mb.residual - mb.residual.median()
mb["uncertainty"] = FLOOR_NT + PERCENT * np.abs(mb.data)
d_obs, unc = mb.data.values, mb.uncertainty.values
print(f"{len(mag):,} readings -> {len(mb)} blocks (up to {mb.n_block.max()} readings per block); data {d_obs.min():.0f} … {d_obs.max():.0f} nT; "
      f"uncertainty {unc.min():.0f}–{unc.max():.0f} nT")

12,006 readings -> 496 blocks (up to 418 readings per block); data -557 … 1347 nT; uncertainty 10–77 nT
In [10]:
# 📊 RESULT
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.6), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.5, 1]})
lim = np.percentile(np.abs(d_obs), 99)
sc = axes[0].scatter(mb.e / 1000, mb.n / 1000, c=d_obs, s=8 + 2 * np.sqrt(mb.n_block), cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-lim, vmax=lim, edgecolor="k", linewidth=0.2)
axes[0].set(aspect="equal", xlabel="easting [km]", ylabel="northing [km]", title="Block medians")
plt.colorbar(sc, ax=axes[0], label="nT", shrink=0.8)
axes[1].hist(d_obs, bins=50, color="C0")
axes[1].set(xlabel="residual anomaly [nT]", ylabel="blocks", title="Distribution of the data")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

4 Topography and mesh¶

Exactly the mesh of notebook 06 (all gravity and magnetic data plus 1 km; 400 m × 400 m × 100 m core cells), so that density and susceptibility models can be compared and inverted jointly in notebook 08.

In [11]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
CORE_DX_M = 400.0          # horizontal core cell size
CORE_DZ_M = 100.0          # vertical core cell size
N_CORE_Z = 20              # core layers (100 m each) below the top of the mesh
N_PAD_XY, N_PAD_Z = 5, 8   # padding cells, expanding by 1.3
REGION_PAD_M = 1000.0      # margin around all gravity and magnetic data (same mesh in notebooks 06, 07 and 08)
In [12]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
grav_all = W.load_gravity(REPO)
mag_all, FIELD = W.load_magnetics(REPO)
region = W.survey_region(grav_all, mag_all, pad_m=REGION_PAD_M)        # same for both data sets
topo = W.topography(REPO, region)
inside = (topo[:, 0] >= region[0]) & (topo[:, 0] <= region[1]) & (topo[:, 1] >= region[2]) & (topo[:, 1] <= region[3])
z_top = np.ceil(topo[inside, 2].max() / CORE_DZ_M) * CORE_DZ_M
mesh = W.build_mesh(region, dx=CORE_DX_M, dz=CORE_DZ_M, n_core_z=N_CORE_Z, n_pad_xy=N_PAD_XY, n_pad_z=N_PAD_Z, z_top=z_top)
active = W.active_cells(mesh, topo)
n_active = int(active.sum())
print(f"region {(region[1] - region[0]) / 1000:.1f} × {(region[3] - region[2]) / 1000:.1f} km; topography {topo[inside, 2].min():.0f}–{topo[inside, 2].max():.0f} m")
print(f"mesh {mesh.shape_cells} = {mesh.n_cells:,} cells, {n_active:,} active (below the topography); "
      f"depth extent {mesh.h[2].sum() / 1000:.1f} km, top at {z_top:.0f} m")

5 Survey, simulation and sensitivity¶

The receivers measure the total-field anomaly (tmi) at the sensor height. The source is a uniform background field with the IGRF strength and direction (UniformBackgroundField). For a scalar susceptibility model the anomaly is again linear, d = G χ, and G is stored in memory. Magnetic kernels decay with the cube of the distance, faster than gravity kernels: the sensitivity weighting matters even more.

In [14]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
receivers = magnetics.receivers.Point(mb[["e", "n", "z"]].values, components="tmi")
source = magnetics.sources.UniformBackgroundField(receiver_list=[receivers], amplitude=FIELD["F"], inclination=FIELD["I"], declination=FIELD["D"])
survey = magnetics.survey.Survey(source)
model_map = maps.IdentityMap(nP=n_active)
sim = magnetics.simulation.Simulation3DIntegral(survey=survey, mesh=mesh, chiMap=model_map, active_cells=active, model_type="scalar",
                                                engine="choclo", store_sensitivities="ram")
tic = time.time()
G = sim.G
sens = np.sqrt((G ** 2).sum(axis=0))
print(f"G: {G.shape[0]} data × {G.shape[1]:,} cells ({G.nbytes / 1e6:.0f} MB) in {time.time() - tic:.1f} s")

G: 496 data × 105,895 cells (210 MB) in 4.2 s
In [15]:
# 📊 RESULT
full = W.model_on_mesh(mesh, active, sens)
v = full.reshape(mesh.shape_cells, order="F")
layer_mean = np.nanmean(v, axis=(0, 1))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.5), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1.4]})
axes[0].semilogx(layer_mean, mesh.cell_centers_z / 1000, "o-", color="C3")
axes[0].set(xlabel="mean sensitivity of the layer [nT per SI]", ylabel="elevation [km]", title="Sensitivity decays with depth")
x, y, s0, z0 = W.depth_slice(mesh, full, 0.0, 0.0)
m = axes[1].pcolormesh(x / 1000, y / 1000, np.log10(s0), cmap="viridis", shading="auto")
axes[1].plot(mb.e / 1000, mb.n / 1000, "w.", ms=1.5)
axes[1].set(aspect="equal", xlim=(region[0] / 1000, region[1] / 1000), ylim=(region[2] / 1000, region[3] / 1000),
            title=f"log₁₀ sensitivity at {z0:.0f} m elevation", xlabel="easting [km]", ylabel="northing [km]")
plt.colorbar(m, ax=axes[1], shrink=0.8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

6 The inversion¶

The same objective function as for gravity, φ = φ_d + β φ_m, with a smallness and smoothness regularisation weighted by the sensitivities. Susceptibility is bounded to BOUNDS (χ ≥ 0): rocks are not diamagnetic at a measurable level, and the bound sharpens the model considerably. ProjectedGNCG respects the bounds; β is cooled until the data are fitted to their uncertainties.

In [16]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
ALPHA_S, ALPHA_X, ALPHA_Y, ALPHA_Z = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
BOUNDS = (0.0, 1.0)       # SI
BETA0_RATIO = 10.0
COOLING_FACTOR = 2.0
CHI_FACTOR = 1.0
MAX_ITER = 25
In [17]:
# ▶ PROCESSING
dobj = data.Data(survey, dobs=d_obs, standard_deviation=unc)
dmis = data_misfit.L2DataMisfit(data=dobj, simulation=sim)
reg = regularization.WeightedLeastSquares(mesh, active_cells=active, mapping=model_map,
                                          alpha_s=ALPHA_S, alpha_x=ALPHA_X, alpha_y=ALPHA_Y, alpha_z=ALPHA_Z)
opt = optimization.ProjectedGNCG(maxIter=MAX_ITER, lower=BOUNDS[0], upper=BOUNDS[1], maxIterLS=20, cg_maxiter=30, cg_rtol=1e-3)
inv_prob = inverse_problem.BaseInvProblem(dmis, reg, opt)
log = W.iteration_log()
directive_list = [directives.UpdateSensitivityWeights(every_iteration=False),
                  directives.BetaEstimate_ByEig(beta0_ratio=BETA0_RATIO, random_seed=0),
                  directives.BetaSchedule(coolingFactor=COOLING_FACTOR, coolingRate=1),
                  directives.UpdatePreconditioner(),
                  directives.TargetMisfit(chifact=CHI_FACTOR), log]
tic = time.time()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    chi = inversion.BaseInversion(inv_prob, directiveList=directive_list).run(np.full(n_active, 1e-4))
seconds = time.time() - tic
d_pred = sim.dpred(chi)
print(f"{len(log.rows)} iterations in {seconds:.0f} s; φ_d = {log.rows[-1]['phi_d']:.0f} (target {CHI_FACTOR * len(d_obs):.0f}); "
      f"χ {chi.min():.4f} … {chi.max():.4f} SI")
log.table

Observed and predicted anomaly and the normalised residuals.

      f"{np.mean(np.abs(nres) < 2) * 100:.0f} % of the normalised residuals within ±2")

8 The susceptibility model¶

Slices at fixed elevations (blank where no data point lies within MASK_M) and vertical sections, among them the north–south section through the strongest anomaly in the south-west (notebook 05). The last figure compares the shallow susceptibility with the reduced-to-pole map of the magnetic chain: an induced, vertically magnetised body produces its RTP high right above it.

In [21]:
# ✏️ PARAMETERS – edit and re-run from here
SLICE_ELEVATIONS_M = (0.0, -600.0, -1500.0)
SECTIONS = {"S–N through the SW anomaly (notebook 05)": ((34.749, 24.700), (34.749, 24.752)),
            "W–E": ((34.70, 24.765), (35.00, 24.765)),
            "A–B (notebook 04)": ((34.7448, 24.7058), (34.9490, 24.8117))}
SECTION_ZMIN_M = -2500.0
MASK_M = 2500.0           # slices: blank cells farther than this from any data point (unconstrained)

# ▶ PROCESSING
np.savez_compressed(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "magnetic_model.npz"), chi_SI=chi, active=active, hx=mesh.h[0], hy=mesh.h[1],
                    hz=mesh.h[2], origin=mesh.origin, data_xyz=mb[["e", "n", "z"]].values, data_nT=d_obs, predicted_nT=d_pred,
                    uncertainty_nT=unc, field=[FIELD["F"], FIELD["I"], FIELD["D"]])
files = W.save_ubc(mesh, {"susceptibility_SI": chi_full}, os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "ubc"), "wadi_ghadir_magnetic")
out = mb[["e", "n", "z", "n_block"]].assign(observed_nT=d_obs, predicted_nT=d_pred, uncertainty_nT=unc, normalised_residual=nres)
lon, lat = W.to_lonlat(out.e.values, out.n.values)
out.insert(0, "lat", lat); out.insert(0, "lon", lon)
with open(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "magnetic_data_fit.csv"), "w") as fh:
    fh.write("# Wadi Ghadir SimPEG magnetic inversion (notebook 07), written by Mohamed Sobh, LIAG. TMA minus trend, block medians.\n")
    out.to_csv(fh, index=False, float_format="%.4f")
log.table.to_csv(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "magnetic_iterations.csv"), index=False)
summary = {"written_by": W.AUTHOR, "data": int(len(mb)), "readings": int(len(mag)), "trend_degree": TREND_DEGREE, "block_m": BLOCK_M,
           "uncertainty": {"floor_nT": FLOOR_NT, "percent": PERCENT}, "field": FIELD, "mesh": list(mesh.shape_cells), "active_cells": n_active,
           "iterations": len(log.rows), "seconds": round(seconds, 1), "chi2": float(np.mean(nres ** 2)),
           "rms_nT": float(np.sqrt(np.mean((d_obs - d_pred) ** 2))), "chi_range_SI": [float(chi.min()), float(chi.max())], "bounds": list(BOUNDS)}
json.dump(summary, open(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "magnetic_summary.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print("written:", sorted(f for f in os.listdir(OUT_DIR) if f.startswith("magnetic")), files)
